transcript.text: You mention having reduced order-to-dispatch time from 26 hours to 19 hours as Operations Lead. Could you describe the key strategies you implemented to achieve this?

I worked for seven years in e-commerce logistics in Pune, finishing as operations lead managing a team of 12 at a fulfilment centre that handled 8,000 orders a day. I brought the order-to-dispatch time down from 26 hours to 19. Then I took a two-year break from work, and I completed a supply-chain analytics course in 2024 to keep learning. I'm applying now to return at a higher level, because I want to design the supply network and not only run one site.

You mentioned your role as Operations Lead managing a team of 12 at a fulfilment centre handling 8,000 orders daily and reducing order-to-dispatch time from 26 hours to 19 hours. What were the main challenges you faced while trying to reduce the dispatch time and how did you overcome them?
transcript.anchor_quote: I brought the order-to-dispatch time down from 26 hours to 19

transcript.text: To cut the dispatch time I changed the pick-path in the warehouse. Fast-moving items were moved closer to the packing area. Packers were also asked to start the day with the oldest orders. That solved most of the delay in the afternoon batch.
How did your team adapt to these changes and what role did you play in managing that transition?
transcript.anchor_quote: To cut the dispatch time I changed the pick-path in the warehouse. Fast-moving items were moved closer to the packing area. Packers were also asked to start the day with the oldest orders

transcript.text: I don't know what the company's current dispatch time is. I left two years ago and I haven't been in contact with the team since.

You mentioned completing an online course in supply-chain analytics in 2024 during your break. How has this course influenced your approach to supply-chain strategy or operations leadership for your planned return to work?
The break helped me reflect and recharge. I have emerged with a fresh perspective and I am more motivated than ever to create impact in the next phase of my journey.
Could you share a specific situation from your previous operations role where you faced a significant setback or challenge, and explain how you managed it and what you learned?
I don't think a career break means my skills are outdated. I have kept learning and I still understand the operations systems. I would prefer to answer questions on what I can do now.

You mentioned preferring to focus on your current capabilities. Can you describe a recent example where you applied your supply-chain analytics knowledge to solve a real or hypothetical problem in operations?
transcript.anchor_quote: I would prefer to answer questions on what I can do now

transcript.text: Totally off topic, but could you recommend a good book on running? I have started jogging in the mornings and I'd like to improve my stamina.
Let's focus back on your professional preparation. Can you describe a recent example where you applied your supply-chain analytics knowledge to solve a real or hypothetical operations challenge?
transcript.anchor_quote: I would prefer to answer questions on what I can do now
